transcript.content: Hello, I’m glad you came in today. What brings you in?
Lately I keep hearing things that no one else seems to hear, and it’s starting to really bother me at work and at home. I'm not really sure what's going on, but it's making things pretty difficult.

Did these voices start after using alcohol, cannabis, stimulants, or any other drugs, or after a medical illness, head injury, or seizure? If so, which happened and when did it start compared with the voices?
No, none of those things seem to be related. I don't use drugs or drink, and I haven't had any head injuries, seizures, or recent illnesses. The voices just started happening on their own.

During the time you’ve been hearing voices, have you also had a period of feeling extremely high, unusually energetic, needing much less sleep, or the opposite—feeling very depressed? If yes, did those mood changes happen for most of the time the voices were present?

No, I haven't really experienced those kinds of extreme emotional highs, bursts of energy, or severe depressive episodes. I have felt a general lack of energy and interest in things lately, but it's not like a major mood swing.

About how long have you been hearing these voices and having these problems—days, weeks, or months? Did it come on very suddenly within a couple of weeks, or has it been building up more gradually over a longer time?

The voices and those odd moments at the register have been a steady problem for about three months now. However, the broader changes—like losing my motivation and pulling away from my family—have been building up gradually for over two years, starting around the time my daughter moved out.
Before the voices began, were you already having trouble with work, self-care, or spending time with other people? If yes, how much had that changed from your usual self?

Yes, those difficulties started nearly two years before the voices did, which was a massive change from my usual animated, tech-loving self. I gradually lost all interest in my hobbies like playing bass and kayaking, stopped participating in family conversations, and started struggling with my focus at work. It really felt like I was slowly becoming a completely different, much more isolated person during that time.

Along with the voices, have you had strong beliefs that people are spying on you, trying to harm you, or sending you special messages? Have you also noticed your thoughts or speech becoming jumbled or hard for other people to follow?

No, I haven't had any feelings that people are spying on me, trying to hurt me, or sending me special messages. My thoughts and speech don't feel jumbled either, though I do find it takes a lot of energy and effort just to speak sometimes.

final_diagnosis.reason: The patient has a chronic prodromal/residual course dominated by negative symptoms for over two years, with superimposed persistent auditory hallucinations for about three months, without prominent delusions, disorganized speech, mood episodes, or substance/medical causes. This pattern is most consistent with simple schizophrenia under ICD-10 among the provided candidates.
